33	\subsection*{Sampling Sensitivity Analysis}
34	\label{app:sampling-sensitivity}
35	
36	To assess robustness to decoding hyperparameters, we regenerate Qwen3-1.7B continuation chains under three sampling configurations (the remaining five generators retain their default-configuration data) and re-evaluate the 6-generator LOGO pipeline (Table~\ref{tab:sampling-ablation}).
37

47	\midrule
48	Low        & 0.5 & 0.80 & 0.785 & 0.797 & $-0.694$ \\
49	Default    & 0.7 & 0.90 & 0.788 & 0.799 & $-0.602$ \\

55	The depth signal is robust to moderate sampling variation: low and default configurations differ by at most 0.3\,pp in both 3-class and binary F1, and entropy--depth Spearman correlations remain strongly negative ($\rho \leq -0.60$).
56	At high temperature ($t{=}1.0$, top-$p{=}0.95$), classification degrades by approximately 6\,pp and the entropy--depth correlation collapses to near zero ($\rho = -0.002$).
57	This is consistent with the hypothesis that depth features are shaped by the sampling mechanism (\S\ref{sec:discussion}): elevated temperature injects sufficient randomness to flatten the distributional drift that accumulates across generation steps, effectively masking the depth signal.
58	The practical implication is that depth fingerprinting applies reliably under standard decoding regimes but should not be expected to generalize to high-entropy sampling settings.

11	All depths            & 12{,}299 & 2.335 $\pm$ 0.000 \\
12	Size-matched (random) & 3{,}951  & 2.367 $\pm$ 0.000 \\
13	Depth 0--1 only       & 3{,}951  & 2.387 $\pm$ 0.001 \\
14	Binary-filtered       & 3{,}951  & 2.389 $\pm$ 0.000 \\
15	Depth 0 only          & 797      & 2.681 $\pm$ 0.001 \\
16	\bottomrule
17	\end{tabular}
18	\caption{Downstream fine-tuning perplexity (OLMo-2-0425-1B, mean $\pm$ std across 3 seeds). At equal sample count, random subsampling (2.367) outperforms depth-aware curation (depth 0--1: 2.387, binary-filtered: 2.389).}
19	\label{tab:downstream}
20	\end{table}
21	
22	The results are unambiguous: data quantity dominates depth composition.
23	Training on all 12{,}299 samples yields the lowest perplexity (2.335).
24	At equal sample count ($n$\,=\,3{,}951), random subsampling (2.367) \emph{outperforms} both depth-stratified selection (depth 0--1: 2.387) and binary detection filtering (2.389).
25	Cross-seed variance is below 0.002 across all variants, which confirms the robustness of this null result.
26	
27	Restricting training to human-only text (depth 0, $n$\,=\,797) produces a sharp perplexity increase to 2.681, driven primarily by the 5$\times$ reduction in data volume rather than depth composition per se.
28	
29	\paragraph{Equivalence testing.}
30	We apply a two one-sided $t$-test (TOST) with a $\pm$2\% relative margin (equivalence bounds $\pm$0.047 on the ppl scale) to formally assess whether the depth-aware and random subsampling conditions produce practically indistinguishable perplexity.
31	At equal sample count ($n$\,=\,3{,}951): size-matched (random) ppl\,=\,2.367 vs.\ depth 0--1 ppl\,=\,2.387, $\Delta$\,=\,0.020.
32	TOST confirms equivalence ($p = 1.1 \times 10^{-4}$); the two curation strategies yield practically indistinguishable downstream quality within the $\pm$2\% margin.
33	Cross-seed standard deviation is below 0.001 for both variants.
34	
35	Comparing the full dataset ($n$\,=\,12{,}299, ppl\,=\,2.335) against the depth-filtered subset ($n$\,=\,3{,}951, ppl\,=\,2.387): TOST \emph{rejects} equivalence (minimum equivalence margin\,=\,0.053, exceeding the $\pm$2\% bound), which confirms that data quantity drives perplexity reduction beyond what depth-aware selection can recover.
36	
37	Knowing the generation depth of a document does not, by itself, make it more or less useful for training; at fixed sample count, depth-aware curation is statistically equivalent to uninformed random subsampling.
38	
39	\subsection*{Margin Sensitivity Analysis}
40	
41	To assess the robustness of the equivalence conclusion to margin choice, we repeat the TOST procedure across multiple equivalence margins \cite{lakens_equivalence}, following the recommendation to report sensitivity across plausible bounds rather than relying on a single threshold (Table~\ref{tab:tost-margins}).
42	
43	\begin{table}[h]
44	\centering
45	\small
46	\resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{%
47	\begin{tabular}{llcc}
48	\toprule
49	\textbf{Comparison} & \textbf{Margin} & \textbf{Equiv?} & \textbf{TOST $p$} \\
50	\midrule
51	Full (12{,}299) vs.\ Random (3{,}951) & $\pm$1\% & No & 1.0 \\
52	                                        & $\pm$2\% & Yes & $1 \times 10^{-6}$ \\
53	                                        & $\pm$3\% & Yes & $< 10^{-10}$ \\
54	                                        & $\pm$5\% & Yes & $< 10^{-10}$ \\
55	\midrule
56	Full (12{,}299) vs.\ Depth 0--1 (3{,}951) & $\pm$1\% & No & 1.0 \\
57	                                            & $\pm$2\% & No & 1.0 \\
58	                                            & $\pm$3\% & Yes & $< 10^{-10}$ \\
59	                                            & $\pm$5\% & Yes & $< 10^{-10}$ \\
60	\bottomrule
61	\end{tabular}}
62	\caption{TOST equivalence testing across multiple margins. ``Equiv?'' indicates whether equivalence is established at $\alpha = 0.05$.}
63	\label{tab:tost-margins}
64	\end{table}
65	
66	The full dataset vs.\ random subsample comparison passes equivalence at the $\pm$2\% margin ($p = 10^{-6}$), while the full vs.\ depth 0--1 comparison requires a $\pm$3\% margin.
67	In absolute terms, perplexity differences are small: $\Delta$\,=\,0.032 (full vs.\ random, 1.4\% of baseline) and $\Delta$\,=\,0.052 (full vs.\ depth 0--1, 2.2\% of baseline).
68	
69	Cohen's $d$ values are 86.0 (full vs.\ random) and 119.7 (full vs.\ depth 0--1).
70	These appear large but are unreliable: with only $n$\,=\,3 seeds per condition, the pooled standard deviation is extremely small ($<$0.001), artificially inflating $d$.
71	The inflated effect sizes reflect low seed-level variance (confirming reproducibility) rather than practically meaningful perplexity differences.
72	The TOST framework with pre-specified relative margins provides a more appropriate assessment than Cohen's $d$ in this low-seed regime.
73

2	We evaluate four train$\rightarrow$test temperature conditions using Qwen3-1.7B data regenerated at $t{=}1.0$ (remaining five generators retain $t{=}0.7$).

5	\centering
6	\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{fig_appendix_cross_temp.pdf}

Matched conditions (0.7$\rightarrow$0.7, 1.0$\rightarrow$1.0) outperform cross-temperature transfer, with 0.7$\rightarrow$1.0 showing the largest degradation ($-6.6$\,pp in 3-class F1). (b) Per-generator 3-class F1 heatmap: Qwen3-1.7B shows dramatic degradation under cross-temperature conditions (0.418) while other generators remain stable. The temperature mismatch disproportionately affects the generator whose data was regenerated.}

11	Key observations from the cross-temperature analysis:
12	
13	\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
14	\item \textbf{Matched-temperature robustness}: Both $t{=}0.7$ and $t{=}1.0$ matched conditions yield comparable performance (3-class F1: 0.789 vs.\ 0.726), with the gap attributable to weaker depth signal at high temperature rather than classifier degradation.
15	
16	\item \textbf{Asymmetric transfer}: Training at $t{=}1.0$ and testing at $t{=}0.7$ (F1\,=\,0.791) transfers well, but the reverse (0.7$\rightarrow$1.0, F1\,=\,0.723) degrades. This asymmetry reflects the information structure: features learned from high-variance (high-temperature) data generalize to low-variance settings, but not vice versa.
17	
18	\item \textbf{Generator-specific vulnerability}: Qwen3-1.7B, the only generator with temperature-mismatched test data, drops to F1\,=\,0.418 under cross-temperature conditions while all other generators maintain F1 $>$ 0.76. This confirms that depth features are calibrated to the specific decoding regime.
19	
20	\item \textbf{Binary robustness}: Binary classification (gen-0/1 vs.\ gen-2+) is more robust to temperature mismatch (0.900--0.958 across all conditions) than 3-class. The coarser gen-0 vs.\ machine boundary appears less sensitive to decoding parameters than fine-grained depth discrimination.
21	\end{enumerate}

1	To assess whether depth signal extends beyond handcrafted features, we fine-tune a pretrained language model end-to-end as a depth classifier using QLoRA \cite{qlora}.

We expect 8-generator training to further improve given additional diversity; the comparison direction is preserved.}
5	For 3-class evaluation, we collapse predictions into gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+ post hoc.

24	\paragraph{Results.}
25	QLoRA achieves 3-class LOGO F1\,=\,0.905 ($\pm$0.003), a +11.6\,pp improvement over the XGBoost baseline (0.789).
26	On 5-class evaluation, QLoRA reaches F1\,=\,0.583 ($\pm$0.010) vs.\ 0.501 for XGBoost (+8.2\,pp), with the largest gains at gen-1 (0.796 vs.\ 0.634) and gen-2 (0.413 vs.\ 0.268).

29	\paragraph{Hyperparameter robustness.}
30	A second run with LoRA rank 32 and seed 123 yields 5-class F1\,=\,0.587 ($\pm$0.005) and 3-class F1\,=\,0.905 ($\pm$0.004), which confirms stability across hyperparameter and seed variation ($\Delta < 1$\,pp on both metrics).
31	
32	\paragraph{Implications.}
33	The substantial 3-class improvement demonstrates that raw token embeddings contain depth signal beyond what summary statistics capture; the seven handcrafted features are a strong but lossy compression of the full distributional information.
34	End-to-end fine-tuning exploits token-level patterns (e.g., positional regularities, n-gram repetitions) that aggregate features cannot represent.
35	This confirms that the depth signal documented in our main analysis is real and exploitable beyond engineered features, while the handcrafted approach retains practical advantages: interpretability, computational efficiency (no GPU inference), and the ability to reveal the differential depth response pattern that motivates the task formulation.

## Summary of Experiments/Analyses in the Paper

Based on my thorough search of the paper's tex files, here's what I found:

### 1. **Appendix Sections** (All exist in the paper)
The paper contains extensive appendices covering:
- **Appendix A**: Dataset Stats
- **Appendix B**: Length Confound Analysis
- **Appendix C**: Prompt Type Generalization
- **Appendix D**: Finer-Grained (5-class) Depth Classification
- **Appendix E**: End-to-End Depth Classification (QLoRA)
- **Appendix F**: Leave-One-Feature-Out (LOFO) Analysis
- **Appendix G**: Confusion Matrix
- **Appendix H**: Classifier Sensitivity
- **Appendix I**: Robustness to Text Perturbation (Human Editing)
- **Appendix J**: Cross-Domain Generalization
- **Appendix K**: Error Analysis of Binary Classification
- **Appendix L**: Downstream Utility
- **Appendix M**: Cross-Model Chain Per-Class Detail
- **Appendix N**: Feature Distribution Analysis
- **Appendix O**: Cross-Temperature Transfer
- **Appendix P**: Feature Ablation
- **Appendix Q**: Feature Correlation
- **Appendix R**: Cross-Family Reference Models

### 2. **Downstream Experiments** - YES, PRESENT
- **Location**: Appendix L (appendix_downstream.tex)
- **Experiment**: Fine-tuning OLMo-2-0425-1B on five data variants (3 seeds each) evaluating perplexity on held-out test set
- **Variants tested**: All depths, size-matched random, depth 0-1 only, binary-filtered, depth 0 only
- **Key finding**: At equal sample count, random subsampling outperforms depth-aware curation

### 3. **Detector Baselines** - YES, PRESENT
- **Detectors included**:
  - FastDetectGPT (referenced as fast_detectgpt)
  - Binoculars
  - LD-Score
  - Avg-LogProb
- **Location**: Main paper results section and appendices
- **Comparison**: All four baselines are repurposed as depth predictors using the same XGBoost framework

### 4. **Cross-Temperature Transfer** - YES, PRESENT
- **Location**: Appendix O (appendix_cross_temp.tex)
- **Experiment**: Evaluates four train→test temperature conditions with Qwen3-1.7B data regenerated at t=1.0
- **Key findings**: 
  - Asymmetric transfer (t=1.0→t=0.7 transfers well, reverse degrades)
  - Generator-specific vulnerability at mismatched temperatures
  - Binary classification more robust than 3-class to temperature mismatch

### 5. **End-to-End Classifier** - YES, PRESENT
- **Location**: Appendix E (appendix_qlora.tex)
- **Method**: QLoRA fine-tuning of Qwen3-0.6B as depth classifier
- **Results**: 3-class LOGO F1=0.905 (vs. XGBoost 0.789), 5-class F1=0.583 (vs. XGBoost 0.501)

### 6. **Distributional Test (TOST) / Equivalence Testing** - YES, PRESENT
- **Location**: Appendix L (appendix_downstream.tex)
- **Method**: Two one-sided t-test (TOST) with ±2% relative margin
- **Results**: Confirms equivalence of depth-aware and random subsampling at fixed sample count
- **Margin sensitivity analysis**: Tests across multiple equivalence margins (±1%, ±2%, ±3%, ±5%)

### 7. **Ordinal Baseline** - YES, DISCUSSED
- **Location**: Appendix D (appendix_finer_depth.tex) and Appendix H (appendix_classifier.tex)
- **Methods tested**: CORAL ordinal regression, Frank-Hall ordinal reduction

- **Discussion**: Paper explicitly studies "non-paraphrastic continuation chains" and references concurrent work on paraphrasing/translation chains
- **Key distinction**: The paper focuses on continuation chains WITHOUT semantic anchoring (unlike paraphrastic chains which preserve semantics)

import argparse
import json
import math
import os

import torch
from torch.utils.data import Dataset
from transformers import (
    AutoModelForCausalLM,
    AutoTokenizer,
    Trainer,
    TrainingArguments,
    set_seed,
)


class TextDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, path, tokenizer, max_length=512):
        self.encodings = []
        with open(path) as f:
            for line in f:
                text = json.loads(line)["text"]
                enc = tokenizer(
                    text, truncation=True, max_length=max_length,
                    padding="max_length", return_tensors="pt",
                )
                input_ids = enc["input_ids"].squeeze(0)
                attn_mask = enc["attention_mask"].squeeze(0)
                labels = input_ids.clone()
                labels[attn_mask == 0] = -100
                self.encodings.append((input_ids, attn_mask, labels))

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.encodings)

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        input_ids, attn_mask, labels = self.encodings[idx]
        return {
            "input_ids": input_ids,
            "attention_mask": attn_mask,
            "labels": labels,
        }


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--model-path", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--train-data", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--eval-data", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    parser.add_argument("--max-length", type=int, default=512)
    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=4)
    parser.add_argument("--grad-accum", type=int, default=4)
    parser.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=2e-5)
    parser.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=3)
    parser.add_argument("--warmup-ratio", type=float, default=0.1)
    parser.add_argument("--eval-steps", type=int, default=100)
    parser.add_argument("--save-steps", type=int, default=500)
    parser.add_argument("--logging-steps", type=int, default=20)
    parser.add_argument("--fp16", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--bf16", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Run 1 step and exit")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    print(f"Model: {args.model_path}")
    print(f"Train: {args.train_data}")
    print(f"Eval:  {args.eval_data}")
    print(f"Seed:  {args.seed}")
    print(f"Batch: {args.batch_size} x {args.grad_accum} accum")
    print(f"LR: {args.lr}, Epochs: {args.epochs}")

        args.model_path, trust_remote_code=True,
        dtype=torch.bfloat16 if args.bf16 else (torch.float16 if args.fp16 else torch.float32),
    )

    print("Loading datasets...")
    train_dataset = TextDataset(args.train_data, tokenizer, args.max_length)
    eval_dataset = TextDataset(args.eval_data, tokenizer, args.max_length)
    print(f"Train: {len(train_dataset)}, Eval: {len(eval_dataset)}")

    max_steps = 1 if args.dry_run else -1
    num_epochs = 1 if args.dry_run else args.epochs

    training_args = TrainingArguments(
        output_dir=args.output_dir,
        num_train_epochs=num_epochs,
        max_steps=max_steps,
        per_device_train_batch_size=args.batch_size,
        per_device_eval_batch_size=args.batch_size,
        gradient_accumulation_steps=args.grad_accum,
        learning_rate=args.lr,
        warmup_ratio=args.warmup_ratio,
        weight_decay=0.01,
        eval_strategy="steps" if not args.dry_run else "no",
        eval_steps=args.eval_steps,
        save_strategy="no",
        # save_steps disabled
        logging_steps=args.logging_steps if not args.dry_run else 1,
        # save_total_limit disabled
        load_best_model_at_end=False,
        metric_for_best_model="eval_loss",
        greater_is_better=False,
        fp16=args.fp16,
        bf16=args.bf16,
        report_to="none",
        seed=args.seed,
        dataloader_pin_memory=True,
        remove_unused_columns=False,
    )

        eval_dataset=eval_dataset,

        trainer.train()
        print("Dry run OK")

    print("\n=== Training ===")

    metrics = trainer.evaluate()
    ppl = math.exp(metrics["eval_loss"])
    print(f"Eval loss: {metrics['eval_loss']:.4f}")
    print(f"Eval perplexity: {ppl:.2f}")

    results = {
        "model_path": args.model_path,
        "train_data": args.train_data,
        "eval_data": args.eval_data,
        "seed": args.seed,
        "eval_loss": metrics["eval_loss"],

        "lr": args.lr,

        "grad_accum": args.grad_accum,
    }

    with open(results_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(results, f, indent=2)
    print(f"Results -> {results_path}")

{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": """"S2 Location Shift distributional tests: KS (pairwise) + Levene (3-group) on 3-class depth grouping."""

import json
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
from pathlib import Path

DATA_PATH = Path("/root/gen-depth-fingerprint/data/features_all_models.csv")
OUT_PATH = Path("/root/gen-depth-fingerprint/results/distributional_tests.json")
OUT_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

FEATURES = ["entropy_mean", "entropy_std", "entropy_min", "entropy_max", "tail_decay", "ttr", "hapax_ratio"]
PAIRS = [("gen0", "gen1"), ("gen0", "gen2plus"), ("gen1", "gen2plus")]
N_KS_TESTS = len(FEATURES) * len(PAIRS)  # 21
ALPHA = 0.05

df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)

groups = {
    "gen0": df[df["depth"] == 0],
    "gen1": df[df["depth"] == 1],
    "gen2plus": df[df["depth"] >= 2],
}

n_samples = {k: len(v) for k, v in groups.items()}

ks_results = {}
for feat in FEATURES:
    ks_results[feat] = {}
    for g1, g2 in PAIRS:
        stat, p = stats.ks_2samp(groups[g1][feat].dropna(), groups[g2][feat].dropna())
        p_corr = min(p * N_KS_TESTS, 1.0)
        ks_results[feat][f"{g1}_vs_{g2}"] = {
            "statistic": round(stat, 6),
            "p_value": float(f"{p:.6e}"),
            "p_corrected": float(f"{p_corr:.6e}"),
            "significant": bool(p_corr < ALPHA),
        }

levene_results = {}
for feat in FEATURES:
    stat, p = stats.levene(
        groups["gen0"][feat].dropna(),
        groups["gen1"][feat].dropna(),
        groups["gen2plus"][feat].dropna(),
    )
    levene_results[feat] = {
        "statistic": round(stat, 6),
        "p_value": float(f"{p:.6e}"),
        "significant": bool(p < ALPHA),
    }

# Summary classification
location_shift_shape_preserved = []
location_shift_shape_shift = []
no_shift = []

for feat in FEATURES:
    any_ks_sig = any(ks_results[feat][f"{g1}_vs_{g2}"]["significant"] for g1, g2 in PAIRS)
    levene_sig = levene_results[feat]["significant"]

    if any_ks_sig and not levene_sig:
        location_shift_shape_preserved.append(feat)
    elif any_ks_sig and levene_sig:
        location_shift_shape_shift.append(feat)
    else:
        no_shift.append(feat)

output = {
    "experiment": "distributional_tests_s2",
    "date": "2026-05-17",
    "n_samples": n_samples,
    "ks_tests": ks_results,
    "levene_tests": levene_results,
    "summary": {
        "location_shift_shape_preserved": location_shift_shape_preserved,
        "location_shift_shape_shift": location_shift_shape_shift,
        "no_shift": no_shift,
    },
}

with open(OUT_PATH, "w") as f:
    json.dump(output, f, indent=2)

# Print summary
print(f"N samples: gen0={n_samples['gen0']}, gen1={n_samples['gen1']}, gen2plus={n_samples['gen2plus']}")
print(f"\nBonferroni correction: {N_KS_TESTS} tests, alpha={ALPHA}")
print("\n=== KS Tests (pairwise, corrected p) ===")
for feat in FEATURES:
    sigs = []
    for g1, g2 in PAIRS:
        r = ks_results[feat][f"{g1}_vs_{g2}"]
        marker = "*" if r["significant"] else " "
        sigs.append(f"  {g1} vs {g2}: D={r['statistic']:.4f}, p_corr={r['p_corrected']:.2e} {marker}")
    print(f"\n{feat}:")
    for s in sigs:
        print(s)

print("\n=== Levene's Tests (3-group) ===")
for feat in FEATURES:
    r = levene_results[feat]
    marker = "*" if r["significant"] else " "
    print(f"  {feat}: W={r['statistic']:.4f}, p={r['p_value']:.2e} {marker}")

print("\n=== Summary Classification ===")
print(f"  Location shift + shape preserved: {location_shift_shape_preserved}")
print(f"  Location shift + shape shift:     {location_shift_shape_shift}")
print(f"  No shift:                         {no_shift}")
print(f"\nResults saved to {OUT_PATH}")

"""Build depth-stratified training datasets for downstream utility experiment.

Pools generation data from all generators, deduplicates depth-0 (same human seed),

"""

import json
import os
import random
import argparse
import math
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer


def load_generations(data_dir, generators):
    all_samples = []
    seen_depth0_seeds = set()

    for gen in generators:
        gen_path = Path(data_dir) / gen / "generations.jsonl"
        if not gen_path.exists():
            print(f"Warning: {gen_path} not found, skipping")
            continue

        with open(gen_path) as f:
            for line in f:
                sample = json.loads(line)
                sample["generator"] = gen

                if sample["depth"] == 0:
                    if sample["seed_id"] in seen_depth0_seeds:
                        continue
                    seen_depth0_seeds.add(sample["seed_id"])

                all_samples.append(sample)

    return all_samples


def split_by_seed(samples, test_ratio=0.2, seed=42):
    all_seed_ids = sorted(set(s["seed_id"] for s in samples))
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    rng.shuffle(all_seed_ids)

    n_test = int(len(all_seed_ids) * test_ratio)
    test_seeds = set(all_seed_ids[:n_test])

    train = [s for s in samples if s["seed_id"] not in test_seeds]
    test = [s for s in samples if s["seed_id"] in test_seeds]

    return train, test


def filter_by_depth(samples, max_depth):
    return [s for s in samples if s["depth"] <= max_depth]


def size_matched_sample(samples, target_size, seed=42):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    if len(samples) <= target_size:
        return list(samples)
    return rng.sample(samples, target_size)


def compute_nll_scores(samples, model_path, device="cuda", batch_size=8, max_length=512):
    """Compute mean NLL per token for each sample using a pre-trained model.
    Higher NLL = more surprising = more likely human-written.
    """
    print(f"  Loading scoring model from {model_path}...")
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_path, trust_remote_code=True)
    if tokenizer.pad_token is None:
        tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        model_path, trust_remote_code=True,
        dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map=device,
    )
    model.eval()

    scores = []
    for i in range(0, len(samples), batch_size):
        batch_texts = [s["text"] for s in samples[i:i + batch_size]]
        enc = tokenizer(
            batch_texts, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True,
            max_length=max_length, padding=True,
        ).to(device)

        with torch.no_grad():
            out = model(**enc, labels=enc["input_ids"])
            shift_logits = out.logits[:, :-1, :].contiguous()
            shift_labels = enc["input_ids"][:, 1:].contiguous()
            shift_mask = enc["attention_mask"][:, 1:].contiguous()

            loss_fct = torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss(reduction="none")
            token_losses = loss_fct(
                shift_logits.view(-1, shift_logits.size(-1)),
                shift_labels.view(-1),
            ).view(shift_labels.size())

            masked_losses = token_losses * shift_mask
            mean_nll = masked_losses.sum(dim=1) / shift_mask.sum(dim=1)
            scores.extend(mean_nll.cpu().tolist())

        if (i // batch_size) % 20 == 0:
            print(f"  Scored {min(i + batch_size, len(samples))}/{len(samples)}...")

    del model
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    return scores


def create_binary_baseline(train_all, scores_train, train_d01_size, seed=42):
    """Create binary-filtered variant: keep samples with highest NLL (most human-like).
    Size-matched to depth01 variant.
    """
    indexed = list(zip(scores_train, range(len(train_all))))
    indexed.sort(key=lambda x: -x[0])  # highest NLL first = most human-like
    selected_indices = [idx for _, idx in indexed[:train_d01_size]]
    return [train_all[i] for i in sorted(selected_indices)]

    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        for s in f:
            pass

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build depth-stratified training datasets for downstream utility experiment.

Pools generation data from all generators, deduplicates depth-0 (same human seed),
splits by seed_id, and creates filtered variants for comparison.
"""

import json
import os
import random
import argparse
import math
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer


def load_generations(data_dir, generators):
    all_samples = []
    seen_depth0_seeds = set()

    for gen in generators:
        gen_path = Path(data_dir) / gen / "generations.jsonl"
        if not gen_path.exists():
            print(f"Warning: {gen_path} not found, skipping")
            continue

        with open(gen_path) as f:
            for line in f:
                sample = json.loads(line)
                sample["generator"] = gen

                if sample["depth"] == 0:
                    if sample["seed_id"] in seen_depth0_seeds:
                        continue
                    seen_depth0_seeds.add(sample["seed_id"])

                all_samples.append(sample)

    return all_samples


def split_by_seed(samples, test_ratio=0.2, seed=42):
    all_seed_ids = sorted(set(s["seed_id"] for s in samples))
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    rng.shuffle(all_seed_ids)

    n_test = int(len(all_seed_ids) * test_ratio)
    test_seeds = set(all_seed_ids[:n_test])

    train = [s for s in samples if s["seed_id"] not in test_seeds]
    test = [s for s in samples if s["seed_id"] in test_seeds]

    return train, test


def filter_by_depth(samples, max_depth):
    return [s for s in samples if s["depth"] <= max_depth]


def size_matched_sample(samples, target_size, seed=42):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    if len(samples) <= target_size:
        return list(samples)
    return rng.sample(samples, target_size)


def compute_nll_scores(samples, model_path, device="cuda", batch_size=8, max_length=512):
    """Compute mean NLL per token for each sample using a pre-trained model.
    Higher NLL = more surprising = more likely human-written.
    """
    print(f"  Loading scoring model from {model_path}...")
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_path, trust_remote_code=True)
    if tokenizer.pad_token is None:
        tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        model_path, trust_remote_code=True,
        dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map=device,
    )
    model.eval()

    scores = []
    for i in range(0, len(samples), batch_size):
        batch_texts = [s["text"] for s in samples[i:i + batch_size]]
        enc = tokenizer(
            batch_texts, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True,
            max_length=max_length, padding=True,
        ).to(device)

        with torch.no_grad():
            out = model(**enc, labels=enc["input_ids"])
            shift_logits = out.logits[:, :-1, :].contiguous()
            shift_labels = enc["input_ids"][:, 1:].contiguous()
            shift_mask = enc["attention_mask"][:, 1:].contiguous()

            loss_fct = torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss(reduction="none")
            token_losses = loss_fct(
                shift_logits.view(-1, shift_logits.size(-1)),
                shift_labels.view(-1),
            ).view(shift_labels.size())

            masked_losses = token_losses * shift_mask
            mean_nll = masked_losses.sum(dim=1) / shift_mask.sum(dim=1)
            scores.extend(mean_nll.cpu().tolist())

        if (i // batch_size) % 20 == 0:
            print(f"  Scored {min(i + batch_size, len(samples))}/{len(samples)}...")

    del model
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    return scores


def create_binary_baseline(train_all, scores_train, train_d01_size, seed=42):
    """Create binary-filtered variant: keep samples with highest NLL (most human-like).
    Size-matched to depth01 variant.
    """
    indexed = list(zip(scores_train, range(len(train_all))))
    indexed.sort(key=lambda x: -x[0])
    selected_indices = [idx for _, idx in indexed[:train_d01_size]]
    return [train_all[i] for i in sorted(selected_indices)]


def save_jsonl(samples, path):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        for s in samples:
            f.write(json.dumps(s, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    print(f"  Saved {len(samples)} samples -> {path}")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--data-dir", default="../data")
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", default="../data/downstream")
    parser.add_argument("--generators", nargs="+",
                        default=["olmo-2-1b", "pythia-1b", "qwen3-0.6b", "qwen3-1.7b"])
    parser.add_argument("--test-ratio", type=float, default=0.2)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    parser.add_argument("--model-path", default=None,
                        help="Model path for binary baseline scoring (optional)")
    parser.add_argument("--device", default="cuda")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    print("Loading generation data...")
    all_samples = load_generations(args.data_dir, args.generators)

    depth_counts = defaultdict(int)
    gen_counts = defaultdict(int)
    for s in all_samples:
        depth_counts[s["depth"]] += 1
        gen_counts[s["generator"]] += 1
    print(f"Total samples (deduped depth-0): {len(all_samples)}")
    print(f"Depth distribution: {dict(sorted(depth_counts.items()))}")
    print(f"Generator distribution: {dict(sorted(gen_counts.items()))}")

    print(f"\nSplitting by seed_id (test_ratio={args.test_ratio})...")
    train_all, test_all = split_by_seed(all_samples, args.test_ratio, args.seed)
    print(f"Train: {len(train_all)}, Test: {len(test_all)}")

    save_jsonl(test_all, os.path.join(args.output_dir, "test.jsonl"))

    print("\nVariant: depth0_only")
    train_d0 = filter_by_depth(train_all, 0)
    save_jsonl(train_d0, os.path.join(args.output_dir, "train_depth0_only.jsonl"))

    print("Variant: depth01")
    train_d01 = filter_by_depth(train_all, 1)
    save_jsonl(train_d01, os.path.join(args.output_dir, "train_depth01.jsonl"))

    print("Variant: all")
    save_jsonl(train_all, os.path.join(args.output_dir, "train_all.jsonl"))

    print("Variant: size_matched")
    train_matched = size_matched_sample(train_all, len(train_d01), args.seed)
    save_jsonl(train_matched, os.path.join(args.output_dir, "train_size_matched.jsonl"))

    if args.model_path:
        print("\nVariant: binary_filtered (scoring with model...)")
        scores = compute_nll_scores(train_all, args.model_path, args.device)
        train_binary = create_binary_baseline(train_all, scores, len(train_d01), args.seed)

        depth_dist = defaultdict(int)
        for s in train_binary:
            depth_dist[s["depth"]] += 1
        print(f"  Binary filtered depth distribution: {dict(sorted(depth_dist.items()))}")

        save_jsonl(train_binary, os.path.join(args.output_dir, "train_binary_filtered.jsonl"))

        scores_path = os.path.join(args.output_dir, "nll_scores.json")
        with open(scores_path, "w") as f:
            json.dump(
                [{"idx": i, "nll": s, "depth": train_all[i]["depth"],
                  "generator": train_all[i]["generator"]}
                 for i, s in enumerate(scores)],
                f, indent=2,
            )
        print(f"  NLL scores saved -> {scores_path}")
    else:
        print("\nSkipping binary baseline (no --model-path). Run with --model-path to create it.")

    print("\n=== Dataset Summary ===")
    print(f"{'Variant':<25} {'Train':>8} {'Test':>8}")
    print("-" * 45)
    print(f"{'depth0_only':<25} {len(train_d0):>8} {len(test_all):>8}")
    print(f"{'depth01':<25} {len(train_d01):>8} {len(test_all):>8}")
    print(f"{'all':<25} {len(train_all):>8} {len(test_all):>8}")
    print(f"{'size_matched':<25} {len(train_matched):>8} {len(test_all):>8}")
    if args.model_path:
        print(f"{'binary_filtered':<25} {len(train_binary):>8} {len(test_all):>8}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fine-tune a causal LM on depth-stratified data and measure held-out perplexity.

Usage:
    python finetune_downstream.py \
        --model-path /path/to/OLMo-2-0425-1B \
        --train-data ../data/downstream/train_depth01.jsonl \
        --eval-data ../data/downstream/test.jsonl \
        --output-dir experiments/downstream/depth01_seed42 \
        --seed 42 --bf16
"""

import argparse
import json
import math
import os

import torch
from torch.utils.data import Dataset
from transformers import (
    AutoModelForCausalLM,
    AutoTokenizer,
    Trainer,
    TrainingArguments,
    set_seed,
)


class TextDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, path, tokenizer, max_length=512):
        self.encodings = []
        with open(path) as f:
            for line in f:
                text = json.loads(line)["text"]
                enc = tokenizer(
                    text, truncation=True, max_length=max_length,
                    padding="max_length", return_tensors="pt",
                )
                input_ids = enc["input_ids"].squeeze(0)
                attn_mask = enc["attention_mask"].squeeze(0)
                labels = input_ids.clone()
                labels[attn_mask == 0] = -100
                self.encodings.append((input_ids, attn_mask, labels))

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.encodings)

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        input_ids, attn_mask, labels = self.encodings[idx]
        return {
            "input_ids": input_ids,
            "attention_mask": attn_mask,
            "labels": labels,
        }


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--model-path", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--train-data", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--eval-data", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
    parser.add_argument("--max-length", type=int, default=512)
    parser.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=4)
    parser.add_argument("--grad-accum", type=int, default=4)
    parser.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=2e-5)
    parser.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=3)
    parser.add_argument("--warmup-ratio", type=float, default=0.1)
    parser.add_argument("--eval-steps", type=int, default=100)
    parser.add_argument("--save-steps", type=int, default=500)
    parser.add_argument("--logging-steps", type=int, default=20)
    parser.add_argument("--fp16", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--bf16", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Run 1 step and exit")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    set_seed(args.seed)

    print(f"=== Config ===")
    print(f"Model: {args.model_path}")
    print(f"Train: {args.train_data}")
    print(f"Eval:  {args.eval_data}")
    print(f"Seed:  {args.seed}")
    print(f"Batch: {args.batch_size} x {args.grad_accum} accum")
    print(f"LR: {args.lr}, Epochs: {args.epochs}")

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model_path, trust_remote_code=True)
    if tokenizer.pad_token is None:
        tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token

    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        args.model_path, trust_remote_code=True,
        dtype=torch.bfloat16 if args.bf16 else (torch.float16 if args.fp16 else torch.float32),
    )

    print("Loading datasets...")
    train_dataset = TextDataset(args.train_data, tokenizer, args.max_length)
    eval_dataset = TextDataset(args.eval_data, tokenizer, args.max_length)
    print(f"Train: {len(train_dataset)}, Eval: {len(eval_dataset)}")

    max_steps = 1 if args.dry_run else -1
    num_epochs = 1 if args.dry_run else args.epochs

    training_args = TrainingArguments(
        output_dir=args.output_dir,
        num_train_epochs=num_epochs,
        max_steps=max_steps,
        per_device_train_batch_size=args.batch_size,
        per_device_eval_batch_size=args.batch_size,
        gradient_accumulation_steps=args.grad_accum,
        learning_rate=args.lr,
        warmup_ratio=args.warmup_ratio,
        weight_decay=0.01,
        eval_strategy="steps" if not args.dry_run else "no",
        eval_steps=args.eval_steps,
        save_strategy="no",
        logging_steps=args.logging_steps if not args.dry_run else 1,
        load_best_model_at_end=False,
        metric_for_best_model="eval_loss",
        greater_is_better=False,
        fp16=args.fp16,
        bf16=args.bf16,

    python finetune_downstream.py \

"""

import argparse
import json
import math
import os

import torch
from torch.utils.data import Dataset
from transformers import (
    AutoModelForCausalLM,
    AutoTokenizer,
    Trainer,
    TrainingArguments,
    set_seed,
)


class TextDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, path, tokenizer, max_length=512):
        self.encodings = []
        with open(path) as f:
            for line in f:
                text = json.loads(line)["text"]
                enc = tokenizer(
                    text, truncation=True, max_length=max_length,
                    padding="max_length", return_tensors="pt",
                )
                input_ids = enc["input_ids"].squeeze(0)
                attn_mask = enc["attention_mask"].squeeze(0)
                labels = input_ids.clone()
                labels[attn_mask == 0] = -100
                self.encodings.append((input_ids, attn_mask, labels))

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.encodings)

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        input_ids, attn_mask, labels = self.encodings[idx]
        return {
            "input_ids": input_ids,
            "attention_mask": attn_mask,
            "labels": labels,
        }

    parser.add_argument("--model-path", required=True)

    print(f"Train: {args.train_data}")
    print(f"Eval:  {args.eval_data}")

        logging_steps=args.logging_steps if not args.dry_run else 1,
        load_best_model_at_end=False,
        metric_for_best_model="eval_loss",
        greater_is_better=False,
        fp16=args.fp16,

        dataloader_pin_memory=True,
        remove_unused_columns=False,

"""Bootstrap CI and effect size analysis for downstream fine-tuning experiments."""

import json
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path

np.random.seed(2026)
N_BOOT = 10000

BASE = Path("experiments/downstream")
VARIANTS = {
    "all":              [42, 123, 456],
    "size_matched":     [42, 123, 456],
    "depth01":          [42, 123, 456],
    "binary_filtered":  [42, 123, 456],
    "depth0_only":      [42, 123, 456],
}

data = {}
for v, seeds in VARIANTS.items():
    data[v] = {}
    for s in seeds:
        with open(BASE / f"{v}_seed{s}" / "results.json") as f:
            r = json.load(f)
            data[v][s] = r["eval_perplexity"]

print("=" * 70)
print("DOWNSTREAM BOOTSTRAP CI & EFFECT SIZE ANALYSIS")
print("=" * 70)

print("\n1. PER-VARIANT BOOTSTRAP 95% CI (seed-level, n=3)")
print("-" * 60)
print(f"{'Variant':<20} {'Mean':>8} {'Std':>8} {'Boot 95% CI':>22}  Seeds")
print("-" * 70)

vstats = {}
for v in ["all", "size_matched", "depth01", "binary_filtered", "depth0_only"]:
    vals = np.array([data[v][s] for s in VARIANTS[v]])
    mean = vals.mean()
    std = vals.std(ddof=1)
    boot_means = np.array([
        np.random.choice(vals, size=len(vals), replace=True).mean()
        for _ in range(N_BOOT)
    ])
    ci_lo, ci_hi = np.percentile(boot_means, [2.5, 97.5])
    vstats[v] = dict(mean=mean, std=std, ci_lo=ci_lo, ci_hi=ci_hi, vals=vals)
    seeds_str = ", ".join(f"{x:.4f}" for x in vals)
    print(f"{v:<20} {mean:>8.4f} {std:>8.5f} [{ci_lo:.4f}, {ci_hi:.4f}]  {seeds_str}")

print(f"\nNote: with n=3, bootstrap resamples have only 10 distinct mean values.")
print(f"CIs appear narrow because cross-seed variance is <0.001, not because n is large.")

print("\n\n2. PAIRED BOOTSTRAP TESTS & EFFECT SIZES")
print("-" * 60)

comparisons = [
    ("size_matched", "depth01",          "Size-matched vs Depth 0-1"),
    ("size_matched", "binary_filtered",  "Size-matched vs Binary-filtered"),
    ("depth01",      "binary_filtered",  "Depth 0-1 vs Binary-filtered"),
    ("all",          "size_matched",     "All data vs Size-matched"),
]

results_out = {}
for v1, v2, desc in comparisons:
    vals1 = np.array([data[v1][s] for s in [42, 123, 456]])
    vals2 = np.array([data[v2][s] for s in [42, 123, 456]])
    diffs = vals1 - vals2

    mean_diff = diffs.mean()
    sd_diff = diffs.std(ddof=1)

    boot_diffs = np.array([
        np.random.choice(diffs, size=len(diffs), replace=True).mean()
        for _ in range(N_BOOT)
    ])
    ci_lo, ci_hi = np.percentile(boot_diffs, [2.5, 97.5])

    if mean_diff > 0:
        p = 2 * (boot_diffs <= 0).mean()
    else:
        p = 2 * (boot_diffs >= 0).mean()
    p = min(p, 1.0)

    d = mean_diff / sd_diff if sd_diff > 0 else float('inf')

    df = len(diffs) - 1
    g = d * (1 - 3 / (4 * df - 1))

    sig = ci_lo > 0 or ci_hi < 0

    winner = v1 if mean_diff < 0 else v2

    results_out[(v1, v2)] = dict(
        mean_diff=mean_diff, sd_diff=sd_diff,
        ci_lo=ci_lo, ci_hi=ci_hi, p=p, d=d, g=g, sig=sig
    )

    print(f"\n  {desc}")
    print(f"    Per-seed diffs ({v1} - {v2}): {', '.join(f'{x:+.4f}' for x in diffs)}")
    print(f"    Mean diff:    {mean_diff:+.4f}")
    print(f"    SD(diff):     {sd_diff:.5f}")
    print(f"    Boot 95% CI:  [{ci_lo:+.5f}, {ci_hi:+.5f}]")
    print(f"    Boot p-value: {p:.3f}")
    print(f"    CI excludes 0: {'YES' if sig else 'NO'}")
    print(f"    Cohen's d:    {d:+.1f}")
    print(f"    Hedges' g:    {g:+.1f}")
    print(f"    -> {winner} has lower PPL by {abs(mean_diff):.4f}")

print("\n\n3. NUMBERS FOR PAPER")
print("=" * 70)

sm = vstats["size_matched"]
d01 = vstats["depth01"]
bf = vstats["binary_filtered"]
r = results_out[("size_matched", "depth01")]

print(f"\nSize-matched: {sm['mean']:.3f} (95% boot CI [{sm['ci_lo']:.3f}, {sm['ci_hi']:.3f}])")
print(f"Depth 0-1:    {d01['mean']:.3f} (95% boot CI [{d01['ci_lo']:.3f}, {d01['ci_hi']:.3f}])")
print(f"Binary-filt:  {bf['mean']:.3f} (95% boot CI [{bf['ci_lo']:.3f}, {bf['ci_hi']:.3f}])")
print(f"\nPaired diff (size_matched - depth01): {r['mean_diff']:+.4f}")
print(f"  95% boot CI: [{r['ci_lo']:+.5f}, {r['ci_hi']:+.5f}]")
print(f"  Cohen's d = {r['d']:+.1f}, Hedges' g = {r['g']:+.1f}")
print(f"  (Large d reflects near-zero seed variance, not large practical effect)")
print(f"\nLimitation: n=3 seeds -> only 10 distinct bootstrap means.")
print(f"Document-level bootstrap not possible (no per-sample losses saved).")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""QLoRA fine-tune a language model for depth classification (5-fold stratified CV)."""

import argparse
import json
import os
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch
from torch.utils.data import Dataset
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold
from sklearn.metrics import (
    f1_score,
    confusion_matrix,
    classification_report,
)
from transformers import (
    AutoTokenizer,
    AutoModelForSequenceClassification,
    TrainingArguments,
    Trainer,
    BitsAndBytesConfig,
)
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model, TaskType, prepare_model_for_kbit_training


class DepthDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, encodings, labels):
        self.encodings = encodings
        self.labels = labels

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.labels)

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        item = {k: v[idx] for k, v in self.encodings.items()}
        item["labels"] = self.labels[idx]
        return item


def load_generation_data(data_dir):
    generators = ["pythia-1b", "olmo-2-1b", "qwen3-0.6b", "qwen3-1.7b"]
    texts, depths, models = [], [], []

    for gen in generators:
        fpath = os.path.join(data_dir, gen, "generations.jsonl")
        if not os.path.exists(fpath):
            print(f"  SKIP {gen}: file not found")
            continue
        count = 0
        with open(fpath) as f:
            for line in f:
                rec = json.loads(line)
                texts.append(rec["text"])
                depths.append(rec["depth"])
                models.append(gen)
                count += 1
        print(f"  {gen}: {count} samples")

    print(f"  Total: {len(texts)} samples")
    depth_counts = {}
    for d in depths:
        depth_counts[d] = depth_counts.get(d, 0) + 1
    print(f"  Depth distribution: {dict(sorted(depth_counts.items()))}")
    return texts, depths, models


def map_to_3class(labels):
    return [min(l, 2) for l in labels]


def compute_metrics_fn(eval_pred):
    logits, labels = eval_pred
    preds = np.argmax(logits, axis=-1)
    f1_5 = f1_score(labels, preds, average="macro")
    labels_3 = [min(l, 2) for l in labels]
    preds_3 = [min(p, 2) for p in preds]
    f1_3 = f1_score(labels_3, preds_3, average="macro")
    return {"macro_f1_5class": f1_5, "macro_f1_3class": f1_3}


def run_fold(
    fold_idx,
    train_texts,
    train_labels,
    val_texts,
    val_labels,
    model_name,
    tokenizer,
    max_length,
    batch_size,
    lr,
    epochs,
    device,
    output_dir,
):
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print(f"FOLD {fold_idx + 1}")
    print(f"  Train: {len(train_texts)}, Val: {len(val_texts)}")
    print(f"{'='*60}")

    train_enc = tokenizer(
        train_texts,
        truncation=True,
        padding="max_length",
        max_length=max_length,
        return_tensors="pt",
    )
    val_enc = tokenizer(
        val_texts,
        truncation=True,
        padding="max_length",
        max_length=max_length,
        return_tensors="pt",
    )

    train_ds = DepthDataset(train_enc, torch.tensor(train_labels, dtype=torch.long))
    val_ds = DepthDataset(val_enc, torch.tensor(val_labels, dtype=torch.long))

    bnb_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(
        load_in_4bit=True,
        bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",
        bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True,
    )

    model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(
        model_name,
        num_labels=5,
        quantization_config=bnb_config,
        device_map={"": device},
        torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    )
    model.config.pad_token_id = tokenizer.pad_token_id

    model = prepare_model_for_kbit_training(model)

    lora_config = LoraConfig(
        task_type=TaskType.SEQ_CLS,
        r=32,
        lora_alpha=64,
        lora_dropout=0.05,
        target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"],
    )
    model = get_peft_model(model, lora_config)
    model.print_trainable_parameters()

    fold_dir = os.path.join(output_dir, f"fold_{fold_idx}")
    warmup_steps = int(0.1 * (len(train_ds) // batch_size) * epochs)

    training_args = TrainingArguments(
        output_dir=fold_dir,

    def __init__(self, encodings, labels):
        self.encodings = encodings
        self.labels = labels

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.labels)

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        item = {k: v[idx] for k, v in self.encodings.items()}
        item["labels"] = self.labels[idx]
        return item

    generators = ["pythia-1b", "olmo-2-1b", "qwen3-0.6b", "qwen3-1.7b"]

        fpath = os.path.join(data_dir, gen, "generations.jsonl")
        if not os.path.exists(fpath):
            print(f"  SKIP {gen}: file not found")
            continue
        count = 0
        with open(fpath) as f:
            for line in f:
                rec = json.loads(line)
                texts.append(rec["text"])
                depths.append(rec["depth"])
                models.append(gen)
                count += 1
        print(f"  {gen}: {count} samples")

    print(f"  Total: {len(texts)} samples")
    depth_counts = {}
    for d in depths:

"""Cross-Temperature Transfer Evaluation.

Evaluates whether an XGBoost depth classifier trained at one sampling
temperature generalises to text generated at a different temperature.

Input:
  - ../data/features_all_models.csv          (generators at t=0.7)
  - ../data/features_qwen3-1.7b-high-temp.csv (qwen3-1.7b at t=1.0)

Output:
  - results/cross_temp_transfer.json

Method:
  Construct two datasets that differ only in qwen3-1.7b's temperature
  (0.7 vs 1.0). For each (train_temp, test_temp) pair, run LOGO-CV:
  hold out one generator, train on the remaining from the training-
  temperature dataset (class-balanced), test on the held-out generator
  from the test-temperature dataset. Average macro-F1 across all folds.

Dependencies: pandas, numpy, sklearn, xgboost
"""

import json
import os
from datetime import date

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, f1_score
from xgboost import XGBClassifier

FEATURES = [
    "entropy_mean", "entropy_std", "entropy_min", "entropy_max",
    "tail_decay", "ttr", "hapax_ratio",
]
CLASS_MAP_3 = {0: 0, 1: 1, 2: 2, 3: 2, 4: 2}
CLASS_MAP_BIN = {0: 0, 1: 1, 2: 1, 3: 1, 4: 1}

XGB_PARAMS = dict(
    n_estimators=200, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.1,
    random_state=42, eval_metric="mlogloss", use_label_encoder=False,
)

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DATA_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "..", "data")
RESULTS_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "results")


def load_datasets():
    """Build two datasets: D_0.7 and D_1.0."""
    cols = ["model_name", "seed_id", "depth"] + FEATURES

    df_07 = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "features_all_models.csv"))[cols]
    df_high = pd.read_csv(
        os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "features_qwen3-1.7b-high-temp.csv")
    )[cols]

    other_gens = df_07[df_07["model_name"] != "qwen3-1.7b"].copy()
    df_10 = pd.concat([other_gens, df_high], ignore_index=True)

    return df_07, df_10


def downsample(df, label_col, rng):
    """Class-balanced downsampling to the smallest class."""
    counts = df[label_col].value_counts()
    min_n = counts.min()
    parts = [
        df[df[label_col] == lbl].sample(n=min_n, random_state=rng, replace=False)
        for lbl in sorted(counts.index)
    ]
    return pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True)

"""Cross-Temperature Transfer Evaluation.

Evaluates whether an XGBoost depth classifier trained at one sampling
temperature generalises to text generated at a different temperature.

Input:
  - ../data/features_all_models.csv          (generators at t=0.7)
  - ../data/features_qwen3-1.7b-high-temp.csv (qwen3-1.7b at t=1.0)

Output:
  - results/cross_temp_transfer.json

Method:
  Construct two datasets that differ only in qwen3-1.7b's temperature
  (0.7 vs 1.0). For each (train_temp, test_temp) pair, run LOGO-CV:
  hold out one generator, train on the remaining from the training-
  temperature dataset (class-balanced), test on the held-out generator
  from the test-temperature dataset. Average macro-F1 across all folds.

Dependencies: pandas, numpy, sklearn, xgboost
"""

import json
import os
from datetime import date

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

FEATURES = [
    "entropy_mean", "entropy_std", "entropy_min", "entropy_max",
    "tail_decay", "ttr", "hapax_ratio",
]
CLASS_MAP_3 = {0: 0, 1: 1, 2: 2, 3: 2, 4: 2}
CLASS_MAP_BIN = {0: 0, 1: 1, 2: 1, 3: 1, 4: 1}

    n_estimators=200, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.1,
    random_state=42, eval_metric="mlogloss", use_label_encoder=False,
)

DATA_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "..", "data")
RESULTS_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "results")


def load_datasets():
    """Build two datasets: D_0.7 and D_1.0."""
    cols = ["model_name", "seed_id", "depth"] + FEATURES

    df_07 = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "features_all_models.csv"))[cols]
    df_high = pd.read_csv(
        os.path.join(DATA_DIR, "features_qwen3-1.7b-high-temp.csv")
    )[cols]

    other_gens = df_07[df_07["model_name"] != "qwen3-1.7b"].copy()
    df_10 = pd.concat([other_gens, df_high], ignore_index=True)

    return df_07, df_10


def downsample(df, label_col, rng):
    """Class-balanced downsampling to the smallest class."""
    counts = df[label_col].value_counts()
    min_n = counts.min()
    parts = [
        df[df[label_col] == lbl].sample(n=min_n, random_state=rng, replace=False)
        for lbl in sorted(counts.index)
    ]
    return pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True)


def logo_cv(df_train_full, df_test_full, label_col):
    """LOGO-CV: for each generator, train on the others from df_train_full,
    test on the held-out generator from df_test_full.
    """
    generators = sorted(df_train_full["model_name"].unique())
    rng = np.random.RandomState(42)

    per_gen = {}
    yt_all, yp_all = [], []

    for gen in generators:
        train_df = df_train_full[df_train_full["model_name"] != gen].copy()
        test_df = df_test_full[df_test_full["model_name"] == gen].copy()

            continue

        n_classes = len(train_ds[label_col].unique())
        params = dict(XGB_PARAMS)
        if n_classes == 2:
            params["eval_metric"] = "logloss"
            params["objective"] = "binary:logistic"
        else:
            params["objective"] = "multi:softmax"
            params["num_class"] = n_classes

        clf = XGBClassifier(**params)
        clf.fit(train_ds[FEATURES].values, train_ds[label_col].values)

        yp = clf.predict(test_df[FEATURES].values)
        yt = test_df[label_col].values

        gen_f1 = float(f1_score(yt, yp, average="macro", zero_division=0))
        per_gen[gen] = round(gen_f1, 4)

        yt_all.append(yt)
        yp_all.append(yp)

    yt_cat = np.concatenate(yt_all)
    yp_cat = np.concatenate(yp_all)

    macro_f1 = float(f1_score(yt_cat, yp_cat, average="macro", zero_division=0))

    labels = sorted(set(yt_cat))
    report = classification_report(
        yt_cat, yp_cat, labels=labels, output_dict=True, zero_division=0
    )

    per_class = {}
    for lbl in labels:
        per_class[str(lbl)] = round(report[str(lbl)]["f1-score"], 4)

    return {
        "macro_f1": round(macro_f1, 4),
        "per_generator": per_gen,
        "per_class": per_class,
    }


def run_condition(df_train, df_test, cond_name):
    print(f"\n--- {cond_name} ---")
    df_tr = df_train.copy()

    df_tr["label_3"] = df_tr["depth"].map(CLASS_MAP_3)

    res_3 = logo_cv(df_tr, df_te, "label_3")
    print(f"  3-class macro-F1: {res_3['macro_f1']:.4f}")

    df_tr["label_bin"] = df_tr["depth"].map(CLASS_MAP_BIN)
    df_te["label_bin"] = df_te["depth"].map(CLASS_MAP_BIN)
    res_bin = logo_cv(df_tr, df_te, "label_bin")
    print(f"  Binary  macro-F1: {res_bin['macro_f1']:.4f}")

    print(f"  Per-gen (3-class): {res_3['per_generator']}")

    return {
        "binary_f1": res_bin["macro_f1"],
        "three_class_f1": res_3["macro_f1"],
        "per_class": res_3["per_class"],
        "per_generator_3class": res_3["per_generator"],
        "per_generator_binary": res_bin["per_generator"],
    }


def main():
    print("Loading datasets...")
    df_07, df_10 = load_datasets()

    gens_07 = sorted(df_07["model_name"].unique())
    gens_10 = sorted(df_10["model_name"].unique())
    print(f"D_0.7: {len(df_07)} rows, generators: {gens_07}")
    print(f"D_1.0: {len(df_10)} rows, generators: {gens_10}")

        "1.0_to_1.0": (df_10, df_10),
        "1.0_to_0.7": (df_10, df_07),
    }

    results = {}
    for cond_name, (df_tr, df_te) in conditions.items():
        results[cond_name] = run_condition(df_tr, df_te, cond_name)

    delta_07_bin = results["0.7_to_1.0"]["binary_f1"] - results["0.7_to_0.7"]["binary_f1"]
    delta_07_3c = results["0.7_to_1.0"]["three_class_f1"] - results["0.7_to_0.7"]["three_class_f1"]
    delta_10_bin = results["1.0_to_0.7"]["binary_f1"] - results["1.0_to_1.0"]["binary_f1"]
    delta_10_3c = results["1.0_to_0.7"]["three_class_f1"] - results["1.0_to_1.0"]["three_class_f1"]

    output = {
        "experiment": "cross_temperature_transfer",
        "date": str(date.today()),
        "model": "XGBoost",
        "hyperparams": {"n_estimators": 200, "max_depth": 6},
        "features": FEATURES,
        "method": (
            "LOGO-CV: hold out one generator, train on remaining from "
            "training-temp dataset (class-balanced), test on held-out generator "
            "from test-temp dataset. D_0.7 = features_all_models.csv. "
            "D_1.0 = same generators + qwen3-1.7b at t=1.0."
        ),
        "results": results,
        "data_info": {
            "t07": {
                "path": "data/features_all_models.csv",
                "n_samples": len(df_07),
                "generators": gens_07,
            },

                "path": "data/features_all_models.csv + data/features_qwen3-1.7b-high-temp.csv",
                "n_samples": len(df_10),
                "generators": gens_10,
            },
        },
        "cross_temp_delta": {
            "0.7_train_delta_binary": round(delta_07_bin, 4),

            "1.0_train_delta_binary": round(delta_10_bin, 4),
            "1.0_train_delta_3class": round(delta_10_3c, 4),
        },
    }

    os.makedirs(RESULTS_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    out_path = os.path.join(RESULTS_DIR, "cross_temp_transfer.json")
    with open(out_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(output, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
    print(f"\nSaved: {out_path}")

    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print("SUMMARY")
    print(f"{'='*60}")

"""Location Shift distributional tests: KS (pairwise) + Levene (3-group) on 3-class depth grouping."""

import json
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats
from pathlib import Path

DATA_PATH = Path("../data/features_all_models.csv")
OUT_PATH = Path("results/distributional_tests.json")
OUT_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

FEATURES = ["entropy_mean", "entropy_std", "entropy_min", "entropy_max", "tail_decay", "ttr", "hapax_ratio"]
PAIRS = [("gen0", "gen1"), ("gen0", "gen2plus"), ("gen1", "gen2plus")]
N_KS_TESTS = len(FEATURES) * len(PAIRS)
ALPHA = 0.05

df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)

groups = {
    "gen0": df[df["depth"] == 0],
    "gen1": df[df["depth"] == 1],
    "gen2plus": df[df["depth"] >= 2],
}

n_samples = {k: len(v) for k, v in groups.items()}

ks_results = {}
for feat in FEATURES:
    ks_results[feat] = {}
    for g1, g2 in PAIRS:
        stat, p = stats.ks_2samp(groups[g1][feat].dropna(), groups[g2][feat].dropna())
        p_corr = min(p * N_KS_TESTS, 1.0)
        ks_results[feat][f"{g1}_vs_{g2}"] = {
            "statistic": round(stat, 6),
            "p_value": float(f"{p:.6e}"),
            "p_corrected": float(f"{p_corr:.6e}"),
            "significant": bool(p_corr < ALPHA),
        }

levene_results = {}
for feat in FEATURES:
    stat, p = stats.levene(
        groups["gen0"][feat].dropna(),
        groups["gen1"][feat].dropna(),
        groups["gen2plus"][feat].dropna(),
    )
    levene_results[feat] = {
        "statistic": round(stat, 6),
        "p_value": float(f"{p:.6e}"),
        "significant": bool(p < ALPHA),
    }

location_shift_shape_preserved = []
location_shift_shape_shift = []
no_shift = []

for feat in FEATURES:
    any_ks_sig = any(ks_results[feat][f"{g1}_vs_{g2}"]["significant"] for g1, g2 in PAIRS)
    levene_sig = levene_results[feat]["significant"]

    if any_ks_sig and not levene_sig:
        location_shift_shape_preserved.append(feat)
    elif any_ks_sig and levene_sig:
        location_shift_shape_shift.append(feat)
    else:
        no_shift.append(feat)

output = {
    "experiment": "distributional_tests",
    "n_samples": n_samples,
    "ks_tests": ks_results,
    "levene_tests": levene_results,
    "summary": {
        "location_shift_shape_preserved": location_shift_shape_preserved,
        "location_shift_shape_shift": location_shift_shape_shift,
        "no_shift": no_shift,
    },
}

with open(OUT_PATH, "w") as f:
    json.dump(output, f, indent=2)

print(f"N samples: gen0={n_samples['gen0']}, gen1={n_samples['gen1']}, gen2plus={n_samples['gen2plus']}")
print(f"\nBonferroni correction: {N_KS_TESTS} tests, alpha={ALPHA}")
print("\n=== KS Tests (pairwise, corrected p) ===")
for feat in FEATURES:
    sigs = []
    for g1, g2 in PAIRS:
        r = ks_results[feat][f"{g1}_vs_{g2}"]
        marker = "*" if r["significant"] else " "
        sigs.append(f"  {g1} vs {g2}: D={r['statistic']:.4f}, p_corr={r['p_corrected']:.2e} {marker}")
    print(f"\n{feat}:")
    for s in sigs:
        print(s)

print("\n=== Levene's Tests (3-group) ===")
for feat in FEATURES:
    r = levene_results[feat]
    marker = "*" if r["significant"] else " "
    print(f"  {feat}: W={r['statistic']:.4f}, p={r['p_value']:.2e} {marker}")

print("\n=== Summary Classification ===")
print(f"  Location shift + shape preserved: {location_shift_shape_preserved}")
print(f"  Location shift + shape shift:     {location_shift_shape_shift}")
print(f"  No shift:                         {no_shift}")
print(f"\nResults saved to {OUT_PATH}")

"""TOST (Two One-Sided Tests) equivalence testing for downstream fine-tuning results."""

import json
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

all_data = np.array([2.3348388849917665, 2.3349729068924905, 2.335356366136214])
size_matched = np.array([2.367420224547984, 2.366607856947016, 2.367365333689391])
depth01 = np.array([2.3877152582337495, 2.3868926542907234, 2.386663183991205])


def tost_test(group1, group2, margin):
    """Two One-Sided Tests for equivalence."""
    diff = np.mean(group1) - np.mean(group2)
    se = np.sqrt(np.var(group1, ddof=1)/len(group1) + np.var(group2, ddof=1)/len(group2))
    df = min(len(group1), len(group2)) - 1

    t_upper = (diff - margin) / se
    p_upper = stats.t.cdf(t_upper, df=df)

    t_lower = (diff + margin) / se
    p_lower = 1 - stats.t.cdf(t_lower, df=df)

    p_tost = max(p_upper, p_lower)

    t_crit = stats.t.ppf(0.95, df=df)
    ci_lower = diff - t_crit * se
    ci_upper = diff + t_crit * se

    return {
        "mean_diff": float(diff),
        "se": float(se),
        "df": int(df),
        "t_upper": float(t_upper),
        "p_upper": float(p_upper),
        "t_lower": float(t_lower),
        "p_lower": float(p_lower),
        "p_tost": float(p_tost),
        "equivalent_at_alpha_0.05": bool(p_tost < 0.05),
        "ci_90_lower": float(ci_lower),
        "ci_90_upper": float(ci_upper),
    }


def find_min_margin(group1, group2, alpha=0.05):
    """Binary search for minimum equivalence margin."""
    lo, hi = 0.0001, 1.0
    for _ in range(100):
        mid = (lo + hi) / 2
        result = tost_test(group1, group2, mid)
        if result["p_tost"] < alpha:
            hi = mid
        else:
            lo = mid
    return round((lo + hi) / 2, 6)


groups = {"all_data": all_data, "size_matched": size_matched, "depth01": depth01}
comparisons = [
    ("all_data", "size_matched"),
    ("all_data", "depth01"),
    ("size_matched", "depth01"),
]

results = {
    "summary": {
        name: {"mean": float(np.mean(g)), "std": float(np.std(g, ddof=1)), "values": g.tolist()}
        for name, g in groups.items()
    },
    "comparisons": {}
}

for name1, name2 in comparisons:
    g1, g2 = groups[name1], groups[name2]
    baseline_mean = np.mean(g1)

    comp_key = f"{name1}_vs_{name2}"
    margin_abs = 0.05
    margin_rel = 0.02 * baseline_mean

    results["comparisons"][comp_key] = {
        "absolute_margin_0.05": tost_test(g1, g2, margin_abs),
        "relative_margin_2pct": {
            "margin_value": float(margin_rel),
            **tost_test(g1, g2, margin_rel)
        },
        "min_margin_for_equivalence": float(find_min_margin(g1, g2)),
        "min_margin_pct_of_baseline": float(find_min_margin(g1, g2) / baseline_mean * 100),
    }

with open("results/tost_equivalence.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump(results, f, indent=2)

print("=== TOST Equivalence Test Results ===\n")
for name, s in results["summary"].items():
    print(f"{name}: mean={s['mean']:.6f}, std={s['std']:.6f}")
print()

for comp_key, comp in results["comparisons"].items():
    print(f"--- {comp_key} ---")
    r1 = comp["absolute_margin_0.05"]
    print(f"  d=0.05 (abs): p_TOST={r1['p_tost']:.6f}, equiv={r1['equivalent_at_alpha_0.05']}, 90%CI=[{r1['ci_90_lower']:.6f}, {r1['ci_90_upper']:.6f}]")
    r2 = comp["relative_margin_2pct"]
    print(f"  d=2% (rel={r2['margin_value']:.6f}): p_TOST={r2['p_tost']:.6f}, equiv={r2['equivalent_at_alpha_0.05']}, 90%CI=[{r2['ci_90_lower']:.6f}, {r2['ci_90_upper']:.6f}]")
    print(f"  Min margin for equivalence: {comp['min_margin_for_equivalence']:.6f} ({comp['min_margin_pct_of_baseline']:.3f}% of baseline)")
    print()

`code/` and `data/` are sibling directories under the supplement root. All scripts assume they are run from the `code/` directory and access data via `../data/`.

# Generation Depth Fingerprinting: Code Supplement

Code for reproducing the experiments in "Generation Depth Fingerprinting."

## Requirements

- Python 3.10+
- CUDA-capable GPU (for generation, feature extraction, and end-to-end classifier)
- A reference language model (e.g., EleutherAI/pythia-410m) available locally or via HuggingFace Hub

Install dependencies:

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Directory Structure

`code/` and `data/` are sibling directories under the supplement root. All scripts assume they are run from the `code/` directory and access data via `../data/`.

```
supplement/
├── code/          # Scripts (this directory)
│   ├── README.md
│   ├── generate_chain.py
│   ├── scripts/
│   └── experiments/
└── data/          # Data files (not included due to size; see data/README.md for format)
    ├── README.md
    ├── features_all_models.csv
    └── ...
```

## Data Format

**Features CSV** (`features_all_models.csv`): One row per text sample with columns:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `model_name` | Generator model identifier (e.g., `pythia-2.8b`) |
| `seed_id` | Wikipedia seed text identifier |
| `depth` | Generation depth (0 = human, 1 = first-gen, 2+ = deeper) |
| `entropy_mean` | Mean token-level entropy from reference model |
| `entropy_std` | Std dev of token-level entropy |
| `entropy_min` | Minimum token-level entropy |
| `entropy_max` | Maximum token-level entropy |
| `tail_decay` | Slope of sorted log-prob distribution (ranks 100-1000) |
| `ttr` | Type-token ratio |
| `hapax_ratio` | Proportion of words appearing exactly once |

**Generations JSONL**: One JSON object per line with fields `{"seed_id", "depth", "text", "model_name"}`.

## Reproduction Steps

### 1. Generate continuation chains (depth 0 to 4)

```bash
python generate_chain.py \
    --input ../data/wiki_seed_1000.jsonl \
    --model-path /path/to/generator-model \
    --model-name pythia-2.8b \
    --output-dir ../data/ \
    --device cuda:0
```

Repeat for each generator model. Multi-GPU sharding is supported via `--shard-id` and `--num-shards`.

### 2. Extract features

Extract 7 features (5 reference-model entropy features + 2 surface features) per text:

```bash
python extract_features.py \
    --input ../data/generations.jsonl \
    --output ../data/features.csv \
    --ref-model /path/to/pythia-410m \
    --device cuda:0
```

Alternative JSONL output: use `extract_features_jsonl.py` with the same arguments.

### 3. Train classifier and evaluate

Single-generator 3-class evaluation with Kruskal-Wallis tests:

```bash
python classify_and_eval.py --input ../data/features.csv --output results/mvp_results.json
```

### 4. LOGO evaluation (main results)

8-generator Leave-One-Generator-Out evaluation (3-class and binary):

```bash
python eval_8gen_logo.py
```

## Script Reference

### Core Pipeline

| Script | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `generate_chain.py` | Generate depth-0 to depth-4 continuation chains |
| `extract_features.py` | Extract 7 features from text (CSV output) |
| `extract_features_jsonl.py` | Extract 7 features from text (JSONL output) |
| `classify_and_eval.py` | XGBoost 3-class classification with statistical tests |
| `eval_8gen_logo.py` | 8-generator LOGO evaluation (main paper results) |

### Ablation and Analysis

| Script | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `eval_8gen_finer_depth.py` | 5-class vs 3-class depth granularity (Appendix D) |
| `eval_8gen_sampling_ablation.py` | Training sample size ablation at 25/50/75/100% (Appendix H) |
| `eval_8gen_cross_model_chains.py` | Cross-model chain extension evaluation (Appendix M) |
| `eval_8gen_baselines_pooled.py` | Pooled LOGO with detector baselines (main paper) |
| `cross_temp_transfer.py` | Cross-temperature transfer evaluation (Appendix O) |
| `end_to_end_classifier.py` | QLoRA end-to-end depth classification (Appendix E) |
| `distributional_tests.py` | KS + Levene distributional tests on features (Appendix N) |
| `scripts/lofo_ablation.py` | Leave-one-feature-out ablation (Appendix F) |
| `scripts/alt_classifier_eval.py` | XGBoost vs LogisticRegression vs RandomForest (Appendix H) |
| `scripts/bootstrap_ci_v2.py` | Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals |
| `scripts/tost_equivalence.py` | TOST equivalence testing for downstream results (Appendix L) |

### Robustness and Controls

| Script | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `experiments/human_edit_robustness/run_robustness.py` | Word replacement robustness at 0/5/10/20% (Appendix I) |
| `8gen_length_confound.py` | Length-matched confound control (Appendix B) |
| `benchmark_efficiency.py` | Inference efficiency comparison |

### Downstream Utility (Appendix L)

# Generation Depth Fingerprinting: Code Supplement

Code for reproducing the experiments in "Generation Depth Fingerprinting."

## Requirements

- Python 3.10+
- CUDA-capable GPU (for generation, feature extraction, and end-to-end classifier)
- A reference language model (e.g., EleutherAI/pythia-410m) available locally or via HuggingFace Hub

Install dependencies:

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Directory Structure

`code/` and `data/` are sibling directories under the supplement root. All scripts assume they are run from the `code/` directory and access data via `../data/`.

```
supplement/
├── code/          # Scripts (this directory)
│   ├── README.md
│   ├── generate_chain.py
│   ├── scripts/
│   └── experiments/
└── data/          # Data files (not included due to size; see data/README.md for format)
    ├── README.md
    ├── features_all_models.csv
    └── ...
```

## Data Format

**Features CSV** (`features_all_models.csv`): One row per text sample with columns:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `model_name` | Generator model identifier (e.g., `pythia-2.8b`) |
| `seed_id` | Wikipedia seed text identifier |
| `depth` | Generation depth (0 = human, 1 = first-gen, 2+ = deeper) |
| `entropy_mean` | Mean token-level entropy from reference model |
| `entropy_std` | Std dev of token-level entropy |
| `entropy_min` | Minimum token-level entropy |
| `entropy_max` | Maximum token-level entropy |
| `tail_decay` | Slope of sorted log-prob distribution (ranks 100-1000) |
| `ttr` | Type-token ratio |
| `hapax_ratio` | Proportion of words appearing exactly once |

**Generations JSONL**: One JSON object per line with fields `{"seed_id", "depth", "text", "model_name"}`.

## Reproduction Steps

### 1. Generate continuation chains (depth 0 to 4)

```bash
python generate_chain.py \
    --input ../data/wiki_seed_1000.jsonl \
    --model-path /path/to/generator-model \
    --model-name pythia-2.8b \
    --output-dir ../data/ \
    --device cuda:0
```

Repeat for each generator model. Multi-GPU sharding is supported via `--shard-id` and `--num-shards`.

### 2. Extract features

Extract 7 features (5 reference-model entropy features + 2 surface features) per text:

```bash
python extract_features.py \
    --input ../data/generations.jsonl \
    --output ../data/features.csv \
    --ref-model /path/to/pythia-410m \
    --device cuda:0
```

Alternative JSONL output: use `extract_features_jsonl.py` with the same arguments.

### 3. Train classifier and evaluate

Single-generator 3-class evaluation with Kruskal-Wallis tests:

```bash
python classify_and_eval.py --input ../data/features.csv --output results/mvp_results.json
```

### 4. LOGO evaluation (main results)

8-generator Leave-One-Generator-Out evaluation (3-class and binary):

```bash
python eval_8gen_logo.py
```

### Core Pipeline

|--------|-------------|
| `generate_chain.py` | Generate depth-0 to depth-4 continuation chains |
